changes: Mark books that Goodreads hasn't tagged. A small amber dot now sits on the tag menu's … button on a book's page when its tags didn't come from Goodreads — either it has none yet, or a fallback source tagged it while Goodreads was unavailable. Hovering explains which: "Not yet tagged from Goodreads — current tags came from Hardcover", say. Goodreads gives far richer tags than the other sources, so these are the books where "Fetch from Goodreads" is worth a try when you happen to be looking at one

Pin SQLAlchemy. It was the one library here whose version nothing decided: it arrives underneath Flask-SQLAlchemy, so every image rebuild quietly picked up whatever had been released by then — the next one was going to move it from 2.0.x to 2.1.0 with no change to this project at all. It is now pinned to 2.1.0 like everything else, and that version has been run against the whole test suite and every page of the app before pinning rather than after

Only decode the image formats covers are actually allowed to be. Pillow works out what a file is from its contents rather than its name, and will open more than forty formats by default — so the check on upload extensions only ever governed what got stored, not what got decoded. A cover downloaded from a URL is saved under a guessed extension, and anything unrecognised is guessed as .jpg, so whatever was really inside it chose the decoder. Thumbnailing now reads JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP and refuses everything else whatever the file is called. Every cover already stored is JPEG or PNG, so none lose their thumbnail

Update Pillow to 12.3.0, which fixes CVE-2026-25990, an out-of-bounds write when opening a specially crafted Photoshop file — reachable before now because a downloaded cover was handed to Pillow whatever format it turned out to be. This raises the minimum Python to 3.10; the Docker image already runs 3.12, but a local virtualenv on 3.9 will need rebuilding on a newer Python

Fix the explanation under the genre scan's "books not yet tagged from Goodreads" option printing on top of the option's own label. Pico pulls small print upwards so it sits tight beneath a form field, which is right where the note follows an input and wrong where it follows the label's text, as this one does

Remember which source gave a book its genres, and let the scan go back for the ones Goodreads missed. Until now a book tagged by a fallback while Goodreads was blocked was finished with as far as the scan was concerned — it had tags, so "only scan books with no tags" skipped it for good, and the better tags Goodreads would have given were never collected. The scan's filter is now three choices rather than a checkbox: books with no tags, books not yet tagged from Goodreads, or every book. The middle one covers exactly the gap — anything a fallback tagged, plus anything still untagged — so running it when Goodreads is behaving sweeps up the shallow-tagged books without re-walking the library. Each book's detail page now shows which source its tags came from, next to the tags. Books tagged before this version are credited to Goodreads, since it was the only source until v1.5.0 and that is true of nearly all of them

Look up genres through a chain of three sources, in an order that now depends on what you are doing. Fetching tags for one book tries Goodreads first, then Hardcover, then Google Books: a request or two is affordable for a single book, and Goodreads gives far better tags than either of the others — measured across this library it is the source most of your existing tags came from, while Hardcover reproduces 43% of them and Google Books 9%. A library-wide scan keeps the opposite order, Hardcover then Google Books then Goodreads, because Goodreads stops answering after a handful of requests and a scan is judged on finishing; once it blocks mid-scan it is dropped for the rest of that run

Add Google Books as a third source. It is the only one that reaches the obscure self-published titles, box sets and manga volumes that make up the untagged part of this library — it answered for 15 of those where Hardcover answered for none — but it returns about one broad category per book, most often just "Fiction". Hence last in the chain: worth asking when the better sources have nothing, not worth asking before them. Needs a free GOOGLEBOOKS_TOKEN; without one it is simply skipped. Each source can still be aimed at directly from the book page's tag menu, and the System page now lists all three with what each is good and bad at

Fix four problems found in a whole-application scan. One book failing during a scan used to take the whole run down with it: the error was recorded but the database session was left unusable, so the next book's title could not even be read and the run ended with nothing tagged, behind a message naming neither the book nor the cause. All three scanners now recover and carry on, so one bad book costs you that book. Names with an accented capital — a tag, series or author like Éducation — are now matched case-insensitively the way the rest are; SQLite's own lower() ignores anything outside A-Z, so such a name never matched what was already stored and the app tried to store it twice, which failed. That produced a 500 from Fetch tags, a failed book in a scan, a Replace that reported a tag missing while it sat in the table, and a rename that could slip past its own duplicate check. A scan that carries on after Goodreads blocks it no longer describes books it only managed to check against Hardcover as having no genres listed — they are now marked as unchecked, and the finished run says which source dropped out, which it previously recorded and never showed. And a genre arriving as "Fiction ," no longer becomes a tag with a trailing space sitting next to the real one

Break up the whole-hierarchy genre labels some books were getting tagged with. A handful of Hardcover's records carry a complete BISAC heading as a single genre — "Comics & Graphic Novels / East Asian Style / Manga / General" — which became one unusable tag instead of the two or three real ones inside it. They are now split into their levels, the filler "General" is dropped, and "East Asian Style" folds into Manga, so that example becomes Graphic Novels and Manga. A slash only counts as a separator when it has space around it, so genuine one-word-per-side labels like "FanFic/Trashy" are still left alone. Tags already created from these headings are unaffected and can be tidied with Replace on the System page

Add Replace to tag management, so one tag can be swapped for another everywhere it is used. Rename deliberately refuses a name another tag already holds, which left no way to merge two tags that mean the same thing — exactly the case after Hardcover started adding LGBTQ alongside the older LGBT. Replace moves everything carrying the first tag onto the second and then deletes the first. Books, authors and series all move, not just books, since tags attach to all three and moving only books would have quietly discarded the rest. Anything already carrying both tags keeps just the one, rather than ending up with a duplicate. The confirmation names how many books, authors and series are affected before anything happens, an unknown tag name is refused with what you typed left in the box to correct, and the table refreshes afterwards so the surviving tag's counts are right

Show which genre sources are usable, on the System page. Hardcover being unconfigured was only visible as a greyed-out entry in a menu on an individual book's page, which is a poor place to learn that a deployment is missing a setting — the Genre Scanner section now lists each source in the order it is tried, whether it is ready, and what to do about it if not. The note for Hardcover spells out the trap that prompted this: under Docker the token has to be both listed in the compose file's environment section and given a value in the .env beside it, and having only one of those looks exactly like having neither. The section is also no longer titled "Goodreads Genre Scanner", since Goodreads has been the fallback rather than the source since v1.5.0

Replace the book page's "Fetch tags from Goodreads" with a "Fetch tags" that runs the same chain the System page's scan does — Hardcover first, Goodreads only for what Hardcover doesn't have. Below it sit "Fetch from Hardcover" and "Fetch from Goodreads", for aiming at one source directly: a disappointing result from the default could mean Hardcover has never heard of the book or that Goodreads is refusing to talk, and picking one says which. The menu no longer requires a Goodreads URL on the book — it used to grey itself out without one, which was most of the library; Hardcover needs no URL at all, and the Goodreads option will find and save one the way the scan does. Flash messages now name the source that answered

Say so when the Hardcover token is rejected, rather than reporting it as a book with no genres. An expired or mistyped token looked exactly like Hardcover never having heard of the book, which sends you looking in the wrong place. Asking Hardcover directly now reports the token; the automatic chain still quietly falls through to Goodreads, since a bad token is no reason to stop tagging

Keep Hardcover's LGBTQ genre as it is written, rather than folding it onto the older LGBT tag. LGBTQ is the more standard form, so it is the one worth moving towards; books tagged from Hardcover will carry it from now on. Existing books keep the LGBT tag they already have — the two can be merged from the tag list on the System page whenever you want them consolidated

Get book genres from Hardcover instead of scraping Goodreads for them. Goodreads stops answering after a couple of requests, which was not even enough to tag one newly added book, because finding it took one request and reading its page another. Hardcover is a Goodreads-style community catalogue with a real API, and its search results carry a book's genres already, so a lookup is a single call to a site that isn't trying to block us. The genre scan now asks Hardcover first and only falls back to Goodreads for what Hardcover doesn't have — measured across a 50-book sample of this library that was about three books in five, against the 28% Open Library managed on the same sample. The scan log now shows which source each book's tags came from. Genres are tidied on the way in: Hardcover's wording is mapped onto tags this library already uses (LGBTQ to LGBT, Young Adult Fiction to Young Adult), compound and half-split entries are broken up or dropped, and a label carrying its own explanation no longer becomes a second tag beside the plain one. Needs a free HARDCOVER_TOKEN in .env; without one the scan behaves exactly as it did before

Keep scanning when Goodreads blocks us. A block used to end the whole run, which was right when Goodreads was the only source but throws away most of a scan now that Hardcover covers the majority of it. The run stops asking Goodreads, carries on with Hardcover for everything else, and still reports why Goodreads dropped out. With no Hardcover token configured a block ends the run as before, since nothing else could answer

Stop the genre scan searching Goodreads for books it can already find. Tagging a book took two requests: one to /search to locate it, then one for the book page itself — and the URL the search returned was thrown away, so every later run paid for the same search again. The scan now uses a book's stored Goodreads URL when it has one, and saves the URL it finds when it doesn't. A scan that gets blocked part way through and is re-run no longer repeats the searches it already did, and books the scan has seen once gain a working Update Tags button on their detail page, which until now refused for want of a URL. Searching is the more heavily rate-limited of the two requests, so this roughly halves the Goodreads traffic of a repeat scan

Fix eight problems found in a whole-application scan. Importing an export taken before the match_key change would have re-announced every book in every monitored series: import inserts its rows verbatim, and the migrations that would fix them are keyed on this instance's schema version, which is already current, so they never ran. Data-level migrations are now applied to imported rows inside the import's own transaction, based on the version recorded in the archive. Editing a book that belongs to a bundle no longer wipes its cost, paid, discounts and purchase date — the form hides those fields for a bundled book, so the save was reading them as empty and blanking whatever the book had recorded before it joined the bundle. A bundle itself can no longer be marked as being read: the hero Start Reading button ignored the rule the Reads tab already followed, and the read it created was invisible in the bundle's history while still holding the bundle on the dashboard. Adding a price watch while Amazon is serving a bot challenge now says so instead of returning a 500. A genre or series scan that hits an error outside the per-book handler now stops cleanly instead of leaving the status stuck on 'running', which blocked every later scan until the app restarted. A scan that stopped early — blocked, or stopped by you — now reports itself as stopped at the book it reached, and shows the reason it stopped, rather than filling the progress bar and claiming the whole library was scanned. Cover images whose filenames are non-ASCII keep their file extension, where before they were stored without one and rendered as broken images. Pushover notifications now label the link for the site it actually points at, instead of always saying 'View on Amazon' for what is usually a Goodreads link

Give the app an icon. A shelf of three books on deep navy now shows in the browser tab, in bookmarks, and on the iPhone home screen when you add the app there. The icon ships as a scalable SVG for current desktop browsers, a multi-size .ico for bookmarks and older browsers, and a 180px PNG for the iOS home-screen tile. A web manifest names it “Books” on the home screen and launches it standalone, without the Safari address bar and toolbar wrapped around it

Fix search fields not updating when text arrives any way other than typed keystrokes. The Search page and the Authors and Series list searches listened for key-up events, so swipe typing on a phone, dictation, an autocomplete suggestion and paste-from-menu all filled the box while leaving the results untouched — the search only ran if you went back and typed another character. They now listen for input events, as the rest of the app's search boxes already did. The clear (×) button in those fields now refreshes the results too, where before it emptied the box and left the old results on screen

Series monitoring now reads Amazon series pages as well as Goodreads ones. A series with only an Amazon link was previously unmonitorable: the check needed a Goodreads URL, and failing to work one out reported 'Could not work out a Goodreads URL for this series' even though a perfectly readable Amazon series page was recorded. Checks now try every URL on the series, Goodreads first, and fall back to the other if one can't be read or is blocking requests, so one site's markup drifting doesn't stop a series listed on both. Working a URL out from a book you own is still the fallback when no URL is set at all. New-release notifications link to whichever site the series is listed on rather than always Goodreads

Matching is no longer confused by how a site writes an instalment number: Amazon's 'Title: Book 2' and Goodreads' 'Title #2' are now recognised as the same book. Previously a book you already owned could be announced as a new release purely because the two sites punctuated its title differently. Existing recorded releases are re-keyed on upgrade so nothing is announced twice

Working out a series URL when none is recorded now starts from books you already have a Goodreads or Amazon link for, reading the series straight off that book's page in one request. Previously it always searched Goodreads by title, which depends on the top search result being the right book and quietly finds nothing for anything obscure — even when a book in the series already carried a link naming the series. Searching remains the fallback for books with no link, and a resolved Amazon series page is saved as the series' Amazon URL

Added a second tab to the dashboard showing how the current year has gone: books, series and authors read, pages read, reading pace, the gender split of the authors you read, and what you spent on books bought this year. Each figure is compared against the same stretch of the previous year — its first N days, not the whole year — so a part-finished year isn't held up against a complete one. Aliases count as the author behind them. The year figures are only calculated when that tab is open, so the normal dashboard is unaffected

Block state-changing requests that come from another website. The app has no login, so this isn't about separating users — it stops a malicious page open in your browser from POSTing to the app's address and deleting data or triggering the database-replacing import, which it could previously do without any access to your network. Requests from curl or scripts, which send no Origin or Referer, still work. Also fixes nine endpoints returning a 500 when given an absurdly large number in the URL (SQLite integers are 64-bit, Python's are not); these now return a 400

Fix three problems found in a project scan. A failed read of a series page was treated as an empty series: it recorded no error, so monitoring looked healthy while doing nothing, and because 'no releases recorded' was what marked a series as un-baselined, the next book to appear was filed as backlist and never announced. Series now track baselining explicitly, an unreadable page is reported as an error, and monitored series whose last check failed are flagged on the Series list. Deleting a book now also unlinks any series release pointing at it — the stale link made the release count as owned and hid it from the dashboard permanently. The compose files also no longer hardcode a placeholder SECRET_KEY, which overrode the value from .env and stopped the app's 'not set' startup warning from ever firing; set SECRET_KEY in .env on the production host

Add series monitoring: opt a series in with the 'Monitor for New Books' button and it's checked weekly for newly released books, with a Pushover notification when one appears. The first check quietly records what's already published, so turning it on for a long-running series doesn't announce its whole backlist. Novellas and in-between instalments (#2.5) count as releases. Found books are listed under 'Newly Released' on the dashboard rather than added to the library, each with a Dismiss button for the box sets and foreign editions series pages mix in; if you later add the book yourself the entry links to it and drops off. A series doesn't need a Goodreads URL configured - one is worked out from a book you already own and reused thereafter - and the weekly check refreshes the series' book count while it's there. Checks run one series a minute and back off if a site blocks them

Space out requests to the same site and stop sending self-contradictory headers, to avoid tripping Goodreads' rate-based bot rules. Importing a book and then fetching its tags used to fire several requests at Goodreads within seconds — the batch scanners already paced themselves, but one-off lookups didn't — so all outgoing page fetches now keep a 2 second gap per host. Also drops a Referer that was being sent alongside 'Sec-Fetch-Site: none' (a combination no real browser produces) and refreshes a user-agent that still claimed Chrome 120 from late 2023

Detect when Goodreads or Amazon serve an anti-bot challenge instead of the page, and say so. Previously these came back as HTTP 202 with a tiny challenge body, which passed the success check and then failed to parse — so a temporary block was reported as the same vague 'Could not fetch tags from Goodreads' as a bad URL or a changed page layout. Blocks now report themselves as such (and suggest retrying later), and the Goodreads genre, series count and author info scans stop when they hit one instead of grinding through every remaining item and hammering a site that is already turning them away

Add a Pushover notification priority setting on the System page (Lowest, Low, Normal or High — High bypasses your device's quiet hours). Defaults to Normal and applies to both price-drop alerts and the test notification. Emergency priority is deliberately not offered, since it re-alerts until acknowledged and needs retry/expire values

Make the calendar icon on date fields actually open the date picker. Pico hides the browser's real picker button and paints its own decorative calendar icon in its place, relying on the invisible button lining up underneath — but that alignment depends on the right-hand padding Pico reserves, which the compact form padding added in v1.0.64 collapsed. That left the clickable area sitting beside the icon instead of under it (about 5% overlap), so clicking the icon did nothing and the field became keyboard-entry only. Date inputs now show the browser's real picker button, so the icon you see is the control you click
Hide the empty '— → —' date range on reads that have no start or finish date recorded — those rows now show just the read number and status. Bundle rows keep their child book link

Rework the book detail page around a Book Details / Reading History tab bar below the cover, and redesign the reading history itself: a summary strip (times read, first/last read, average duration), numbered read entries showing status, date range and duration, inline edit that swaps the row in place instead of expanding a nested form, and a compact Add Read button. A last-read (or 'reading since') date now also appears with the other book facts up top. Adding, editing or deleting a read returns you to the Reading History tab, while Start Reading / Mark Complete from the header stays on Book Details

Fix the inactive tab on the book detail page's new tab bar becoming invisible on hover in light mode — Pico redefines its --pico-color variable to white on button hover states, so the fix uses `inherit` instead of reading that variable directly

Add a tabbed 'More in Series' / 'Similar Books' section to the bottom of the book detail page. Similar Books is ranked by number of shared tags and excludes any book already in the same series. Only shows a tab bar when both sections have content; shows a plain heading for whichever one does when only one applies, and nothing at all when neither does

Add a Tags page (sidebar, above Statistics) for browsing books by one or more tags — pick tags from the full tag cloud (each showing its book count) to narrow the results to books with all of the selected tags, add more via a search box, or remove them individually. Tag chips on the book detail page are now clickable links straight into this filtered view
Change the Price Watch icon from a price tag to a dollar sign, in both the sidebar and the page header

Tighten the sidebar's vertical spacing to match the rest of the compact redesign — less padding around the header, nav links, section labels, and footer/theme toggle, in both the expanded and collapsed (icon-only) states

Remove CSS left over from the v1.0.64-71 UI overhaul: the old boxed .meta-info/.meta-item/.meta-label/.meta-value card (replaced by .detail-facts), .dropdown-divider (the book detail page's options menu no longer has an Edit/Delete section to divide), and .detail-tags (replaced by .tags-row/.detail-chip). No visual change — these rules were no longer referenced by any template

Group the author detail page's book grid by series (alphabetical, linked to the series page, with a #N badge on each cover), with a 'Standalone' group for books with no series at the end. Authors with no series at all keep the plain flat grid — no redundant heading

Fix the Queue page's reorder menu (First/Previous/Next/Last) still showing the old, roomier padding — the shared dropdown-menu component only had its spacing tightened for the book detail page; the fix now lives in the shared base rule so every dropdown menu in the app (Queue's reorder menu, the Books list 'Add New Book' options menu, and book detail's menus) is consistently compact
Shorten the Dashboard's 'Mark Complete' button to 'Complete' — the longer label was wrapping to two lines, making it taller than the 'Abandon' button beside it

Extend the compact, Grimmory-inspired redesign to the remaining pages: Dashboard (bordered instead of filled active-read cards, fixed another dead '.small' button class), Statistics (stat tiles now match the Dashboard's plain style, chart/table sections use a subtle border instead of filled Pico cards), System (every settings section similarly bordered, and its many scattered buttons — export/import, tag rename/delete, scan start/pause/stop, theme toggle — are now right-sized instead of full Pico scale), plus smaller consistency passes on the Queue, Recommendations, and Price Watch pages

Fix the Format/Rating dropdowns on the book edit form rendering 1px taller than the Page Count field beside them — v1.0.66 only floored <select>/date-input height, not plain text/number inputs; all edit-form field types now share the same min-height

Fix the reading-status dropdown on the book detail page (and the Format/Rating dropdowns on the edit forms) rendering slightly shorter than the date fields beside it on wide screens — the v1.0.65 min-height fix only covered date inputs, not <select> elements

Fix date input fields on the reading-history and book/author/series edit forms rendering shorter than their own calendar-picker icon on mobile when empty — the v1.0.64 compact redesign reset input height to 'auto' with no floor, so give date fields an explicit minimum height instead

Redesign the book, author, and series detail pages plus their Add/Edit forms with a more compact, Grimmory-inspired look — smaller covers, plain-text metadata instead of boxed cards, pill-shaped tag chips, right-sized buttons and dropdown menus instead of full Pico scale, and a bordered style for Description/Notes sections instead of filled cards. The series detail page now shows its books as a wrapping cover grid (with the book number as a corner badge) instead of a table. Also pins Pico's fluid root font-size scaling, which was quietly re-inflating UI on wide windows, and fixes an unstyled 'small' button class that left Edit buttons oversized on the Series and Author list pages

Harden export/import and thumbnails after a code review: corrupt or incomplete import zips now show an error instead of breaking the System page, import failures (e.g. conflicting data) flash a message instead of a 500 and leave the database unchanged, importing is blocked while an export is building, huge-pixel cover images no longer break book saves or the thumbnail backfill, direct cover uploads are capped at 10MB again, orphaned export temp files are cleaned up at startup, and exports now fail loudly at startup if a new table is missing from the export list

Serve resized cover thumbnails (max 400px wide) on all list and grid pages instead of full-size images — the book detail page lightbox still shows the original. Thumbnails are generated on upload, backfilled in the background at startup, and regenerated after an import. Adds Pillow as a dependency.

Build library exports in the background — the Export Library button now shows a live progress bar while the zip is assembled (helpful on slower hosts), then presents a Download Export button; the built zip is kept for re-download until the next export or app restart

Add full-library export and import to the System page — export downloads a zip of all data (as JSON) plus cover images; importing a zip replaces the instance's data after an explicit confirmation step, backing up the current database to books_pre_import.db first

Fix the author/series suggestion chips on the book form rendering as full-width rows — the author scan review styles (v1.0.54) reused the same CSS class name; the System page rows are now .author-scan-suggestion

Add a book options menu (…) next to the title on the book details page — find the book on Amazon, Goodreads, StoryGraph, or Kobo (linking directly when the book has a stored URL), plus Edit and Delete
Add a Notes field to authors — free-text notes shown on the author page and edited on the author form
Add a 'Male and Female' gender option for two people writing under one pen name
Add an 'Unknown Gender' filter to the Authors page showing authors with no gender set or gender set to Unknown — works alongside search, pagination, and per-page

Fix the author scan's 'Review suggestions' button doing nothing when clicked from the System page — it now loads the review section in place via htmx instead of a same-page anchor link that never triggered a reload
Harden the author scan worker so an unexpected error can't leave the progress display stuck on 'running' forever — it now logs the error to the scan log and stops cleanly

Add Author Gender & Pronoun Scanner to the System page: looks up authors missing gender or pronouns using their Goodreads bio, Wikidata/Wikipedia, and website, counting the pronouns actually used in third-person prose (never guessing from names)
Scan findings appear as suggestions with an evidence quote and source link — accept or reject each one (or Accept All); nothing is written to an author without review
Scan pre-pass syncs gender/pronouns between alias and primary author records automatically
Add a 'Look up gender & pronouns' button to the author form that does the same lookup live and pre-fills the fields with the evidence shown
Fix Amazon cover images being lost during import when the page provides a plain image URL (operator-precedence bug)
Fix Pushover test button reporting success when the API rejected the notification — the API response is now checked
Fix a single failing price watch aborting the daily check for all remaining watches; errors are recorded per watch instead
Fix the price watch scheduler running twice (duplicate checks/notifications) under the Flask debug server
Fix deleting a book leaving a blank ghost entry in the reading queue
Fix 'add to top' of the reading queue assigning duplicate positions once an item reached position 0
Fix starting a genre/series scan while another was paused running two scans at once
Validate that a read's finish date is not before its start date, and that a book has a format, with friendly errors instead of crashes
Harden cover image URL downloads: redirects are re-validated against private/internal addresses and downloads are capped at 10MB
Use local time consistently for date added / created timestamps (was a mix of UTC and local, causing off-by-one-day displays)
Fix quick-add and duplicate checks treating % and _ in names as wildcards, which could match the wrong author/series/tag
Internal: all routes now use blueprint-qualified endpoints; removed the bare-endpoint aliasing shim
Add a 'Send Test Notification' button to the System page when Pushover credentials are configured
Add Kindle Price Watch: track Amazon Kindle book prices and get a Pushover notification when the price drops
New 'Price Watch' page in the sidebar nav for adding/removing watched books and checking prices on demand

Replace the book form's author and series pickers with a live search dropdown instead of a browser datalist, which iOS Safari doesn't support reliably — fixes author/series search not working when editing books on mobile
Fix author search slowness introduced by the new author.alias_of_id index — it had poor selectivity and made SQLite pick a worse query plan; replaced it with an index on author.name instead
Add database indexes on frequently filtered/joined columns (read.book_id, read.status, book.series_id, book.format_id, book.parent_id, book.date_added, author.alias_of_id, reading_queue.book_id)
Fix N+1 queries on the queue, series list, author detail, series detail, book list, and bundle child search pages
Batch the queue reorder update instead of fetching each item individually
Rewrite the Dashboard's Recently Read query to use a bounded aggregate instead of scanning the full reading history
Fix Amazon import failing on some product pages due to a header that was tripping Amazon's bot detection
Add 'Recently Read' section to the Dashboard, below Recently Added
Remove dead code: unused author/series search routes and templates, an orphaned description-scraper route, an unwired bundle quick-add route, and leftover CSS from earlier nav and picker designs
Auto-select Kindle format when importing a book from an Amazon Kindle URL
Add Amazon URL field to books, auto-populated on import alongside Goodreads URL
Automatically strip tracking/search cruft from Goodreads, Amazon, and StoryGraph URLs when saved
Add cache-busting version query to style.css so CSS updates aren't served stale from browser cache
Fix queue split button width not matching other buttons on mobile-width book detail page
Add Goodreads URL field to books
Add '...' menu on book detail tags to fetch missing tags from Goodreads
Fix queue Move dropdown clipping off right edge of viewport
Series update count now checks both Goodreads and Amazon and uses the higher value
Add Move dropdown to queue items for quickly repositioning to First, Previous, Next, or Last
Add 'at top' option to queue button on book detail page via split dropdown
Search results now include books by matching authors in the Books section
Improve Recommendations page load time by batching per-series queries
Allow browser caching of cover images and other static assets, fixing images visibly reloading on every page view
Fix XSS vulnerabilities in tag/author/series/bundle-child pickers and series name check
Add Discounts by Format per Year chart to Statistics page showing Kindle and Kobo discounts
Add book format tag to each reading queue item, displayed inline with the title
Add Spending by Format per Year stacked bar chart to Statistics page
Add Spending by Format summary table with per-year columns and totals
Table scrolls horizontally with the Format column pinned to the left
Add Average Book Cost and Median Book Cost to the Statistics summary
Fix statistics summary stat values being clipped or wrapping on wider number values
Fix content area width jumping on page load when sidebar is collapsed
Fix sidebar flash of expanded state on page load when sidebar is collapsed
Add icon and styled heading to each page header, matching the active sidebar navigation item
Page heading text and icon now use the sidebar active colour
Fix sidebar active link highlighting not working on any page
Replace top navigation bar with a collapsible sidebar — collapses to icon-only mode on desktop, slides in via hamburger on mobile
Sidebar state (collapsed/expanded) persisted in localStorage
Active navigation item highlighted in sidebar
Dark mode toggle moved to sidebar footer
Fix hamburger icon line colour not visible in light mode
Add Books Read per Year bar chart to the Statistics page
Change 'Books Added per Year' statistics chart to 'Books Purchased per Year' using the purchase date
Fix oversized cover image on book detail page on mobile
Fix book detail page cover image being too large on mobile — now shows as a compact side-by-side layout
Fix Escape key on System page tag search not clearing results
Replace deprecated Model.query.get() and get_or_404() with db.session.get() and db.get_or_404()
Pin exact dependency versions in requirements.txt
